title: Encode & ImageBitmap round-trip
blurb: Paints 16x SDR white into float16 srgb-linear canvases, exports via toDataURL, toBlob, convertToBlob, createImageBitmap, and transferToImageBitmap, decodes back, and measures channel preservation across PNG, JPEG, and WebP.
question: Do canvas serialization paths (toDataURL, toBlob, convertToBlob) preserve 16x SDR highlights for 'extended' canvases and clamp to ~1.0 for 'standard' canvases?
result: In Chrome 153 headless across PNG, JPEG, and WebP, all 'standard' encode rows pass (~1.000) while 'extended' encode rows fail at 1.000 (clamped pre-feature behavior); ImageBitmap rows stay informational pending whatwg/html#13235. Native HDR file encoding requires Chrome 160+.
testedIn: Chrome for Testing 153.0.8010.12 (flag off and --enable-experimental-web-platform-features); not verified in Chrome 160

friction.summary: Explicit tone-mapping state tracking on ImageBitmap objects is still unresolved in the HTML specification
friction.repro: Export an extended float16 canvas via createImageBitmap(canvas) or transferToImageBitmap(); there is no specified property or pinned WPT expectation yet for inspecting tone-mapping state on the resulting ImageBitmap.
friction.workaround: Treat ImageBitmap round-trip checks as informational until whatwg/html#13235 defines bitmap state tracking.

friction.summary: Extended float16 canvas exports clamp 16x white down to 1.0 in Chrome 153 even with the experimental flag enabled
friction.repro: Paint color(srgb-linear 16 16 16) on a float16 extended canvas and call convertToBlob({ type: 'image/png' }); decoding back into a float16 canvas reads 1.000 instead of ~16.
friction.workaround: Verify extended reflection before offering HDR image export, or test on Chrome 160+ where HDR PNG/HLG/PQ encoding is wired.
